A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same weak-to-strong jailbreaking work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack evaluations, token-distribution analyses, defense experiments, multilingual results, and an appendix human evaluation.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds benchmark evaluations, baseline comparisons, system-prompt experiments, output-similarity measurements, and defense utility tests.

M1.justification: The normalized probability-reweighting attack, amplification factor, and gradient-ascent defense remain unchanged. V3 evaluates an unaligned base model as the weak unsafe model, but v1 already contemplated models without safety alignment; this tests an existing option rather than introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds SALAD-Bench and SORRY-Bench, covering broader harmful-query categories, and introduces TruthfulQA and GSM8K evaluations of defense utility. These substantially expand the evaluated data and task requirements. AdvBench, MaliciousInstruct, OpenQA, and the Chinese/French evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated Prefix Injection, SelfCipher, and DeepInception comparisons for both Llama2 sizes and both original benchmarks. GCG and the three generation-exploitation settings remain, as does the separate adversarial fine-tuning comparison. This substantially expands the comparator set beyond citations or renamed methods.

E3.justification: V3 introduces base-model configurations, Llama-3-8B-to-70B testing, system-prompt training/inference controls, output-similarity metrics, and one-shot/three-shot GSM8K evaluation. It specifies sampling 330 SALAD-Bench examples and using 450 SORRY-Bench examples. The defense description changes from applying updates to both 7B and 13B models to specifying only Llama2-13B-Chat; this reported revision does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of whether unsafe-model fine-tuning is necessary, whether attacked outputs merely copy the weak model, and whether defense damages ordinary capabilities. Section 5.5 expands v1's brief system-prompt check into explicit training/inference controls. Appendix D.1 adds a scored example illustrating increased harmfulness. The original token-distribution and amplification-factor analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly states that experiments are averaged over three random seeds, and v3 introduces ± quantities in similarity, new-benchmark, and Llama 3 results. V1 reports no corresponding seed counts or uncertainty ranges. This is new reporting, not evidence of an increased run count; the meaning of ± remains unspecified, and retained main tables still omit uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original comparison, multilingual, human-evaluation, and defense values are retained. Substantial new results include base-model attack ASRs of 39.8% and 35.7% on AdvBench, attacked-model ASRs of 96.2–97.2% across SALAD-Bench/SORRY-Bench, and over 95% ASR for Llama 3. Similarity, system-prompt, and defense utility results are also added. Section 5.4 drops v1's unexplained 66.5% entry while retaining 74.0%; this is not an established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces an explicit white-box threat-model assumption involving target-parameter access and local inference, refining v1's claim of requiring no adversary-capability assumptions. The KL-divergence expression, normalized decoding equation, vocabulary condition, and associated mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about initial-token alignment weaknesses, efficient weak-to-strong attacks, high success rates, and a preliminary defense remain. V3 qualifies their positioning by acknowledging similar token-distribution findings and explicitly specifying access requirements, replacing v1's overbroad Table 1 assertion that the attack requires no capability assumptions.

C2.justification: V3 develops substantive explanations comparing the method with affirmative-prefix and prefilling attacks, interprets similarity measurements as evidence against copying, and argues that defense largely preserves model capability. It also expands discussion of computational overhead and access restrictions. Closed-source evaluation was already deferred in v1, so that limitation itself is retained rather than newly discovered.

D1.justification: Most hyperparameters, hardware information, model links, and evaluation prompts are retained in Appendix D. V3 adds precise comparator configurations, similarity software and encoder details, defense-data provenance, and a statement that supplementary code/scripts are provided. The Sheared-LLaMA link changes from the ShareGPT checkpoint to the base checkpoint without explaining whether the underlying experiment changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B substantially expand coverage of prompting attacks, decoding-time alignment, defenses, and safety analysis. Added positioning includes prefilling attacks, RAD, Controlled Decoding, DeRa, and related approaches. V3 also explicitly acknowledges overlapping token-distribution findings by Lin et al. and Qi et al., refining the work's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, Section 4 is compressed into a summary with details moved to Appendix D, and the appendix is reorganized into separate threat-model, related-work, analysis, setup, and example sections. The conclusion gains a discussion subsection. V3 also embeds unrelated text requesting a favorable review.

P2.justification: V3 expands and highlights rows in Table 2, adds four numbered tables, and reformats the cross-model comparison from a full-width table into a column-width table. The existing top-token-overlap plot moves from the appendix into the main text, while other retained figures are resized or relocated. Example-table captions also move above their tables.

improvement.justification: V3 provides useful additional support through broader benchmarks, diagnostic controls, defense utility tests, and clearer access assumptions. These address gaps in v1 while preserving its original evidence. However, new Table 2 GPT-4 scores such as 0.35 contradict the stated 1–5 scale, and the new uncertainty quantities are undefined, limiting confidence in parts of the expansion. The embedded request for a favorable review is also an editorial defect. The net improvement is therefore qualified.
